subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Digital Signatures
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Digital Signatures.

hook.text: How do you prove a message is really from you and hasn't been changed? Digital signatures solve that.

buildup.text: A digital signature uses your private key to create a unique stamp that anyone can verify with your public key.

discovery.text: If even one character of the message changes after signing, the verification fails completely.

twist.text: Digital signatures don't hide the message. They prove who sent it and that nobody tampered with it.

climax.text: Every software update, secure email, and cryptocurrency transaction relies on digital signatures for trust.

punchline.text: Not about hiding. About proving who sent it.

quiz.question: What do digital signatures prove about a message?
options: Who sent it and that it hasn't been tampered with
That the message is encrypted and hidden
That the message was sent at a specific time
